newsitem.title: CHINA: Trade up 10.9 pct in China's booming Guangdong.
newsitem.headline: Trade up 10.9 pct in China's booming Guangdong.

text.p: Foreign trade grew 10.9 percent in China's booming southern Guangdong province in the first two months to $15.26 billion, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
Exports grew 20 percent to $9.0 billion, creating a surplus of $2.72 billion, it said.
Guangdong's foreign trade accounted for 39.8 percent of the national total, it said.
Processing trade totalled $11.18 billion, the main contributor to foreign trade in the province.
Capital goods imported for foreign-funded firms totalled $530 million, down 21.8 percent.
Exports of state-owned firms reached $4.4 billion, up 34.2 percent from a year-ago. Imports rose 4.2 percent to $3.8 billion.
Textiles, light industrial products such as garments, shoes, toys and plastic products remained the major export items.
Major import items included raw materials, plastics, steel, integrated circuits and paper.
Exports to neighbouring Hong Kong accounted for 40 percent of the total.
